title: An exponent changes extrapolation
hook: Compare two stipulated scaling exponents across four doublings.

doesNotKnow: Explain how repeated scale changes magnify disagreements between assumed exponents.

misconception: A modest exponent difference stays a modest absolute disagreement at every scale.
objective: Explain how repeated scale changes magnify disagreements between assumed exponents.

claims.text: Scaling exponents describe how quantities change with system size.
The three-quarter exponent, rounded to 68.18% per doubling, gives {A}; exponent one gives {B}. Four repeated size doublings magnify their disagreement from the common starting value.
claims.source: {"type":"author-derivation","formula":"repeat x=x*(1+rate/100)+addition","inputs":[[1,68.18,4,0],[1,100,4,0]],"outputs":[8.000136417057536,16],"note":"68.18% is 2^(3/4)-1 rounded to 2 dp (implied exponent 0.750006); A displays as 8 at the 2-dp readout"}

claims.text: Does it hold up? Only as power-law arithmetic. No exponent was fitted here, and extrapolation does not verify a biological or urban law.
claims.source: {"type":"source-access-hold","note":"No empirical effect or research verdict established. Only bounded arithmetic proposed."}

recall.question: One model multiplies by 2 per doubling; another by 1.5. After two doublings?
